en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ekāsaniya Mahāparivāra-vagga, Chapter 4, Number 4 I was a monk endowed with supernormal power, possessing great psychic might; I sat upon a single seat for one hundred thousand aeons. Having performed such deeds, I attained the state of an Arhat. Now, having become an Arhat, I sit upon a single seat.
Thus did the Elder Ekāsaniya speak his own ancient account.
“At that time, I was the king of the gods named Varuṇa;
I attended upon the Perfectly Enlightened One.”
Fully equipped with forces and vehicles,
when Atthadassī, the supreme among men and lord of the world, had attained final nibbāna.
Taking all four types of musical instruments,
I went to the supreme Bodhi tree,
accompanied by instrumental music and dance.
Composed as if by a well-beaten drum,
I stood before the supreme Bodhi tree as if in the presence of the Fully Awakened One himself.
Having attended upon that Bodhi tree,
a plant growing from the earth,
and having sat down cross-legged,
There I passed away;
delighted by my own karma,
I was full of faith in the supreme Bodhi.
Through that serene confidence of mind,
I was reborn in the realm of the gods;
sixty thousand musical instruments—
They always surround me,
as I pass through existence after existence among humans and devas.
The threefold fires have been extinguished within me;
all states of existence have been uprooted;
I bear my final body.
In the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
there were thirty-four kṣatriyas known by the name Subāhu.
Endowed with the seven treasures,
five hundred eons from now,
[he will attain] the four analytical knowledges.
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Ekāsaniya Thera speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Ekāsaniya is the fourth.
